verdict.rationale: Gitleaks can scan non-git content through its `dir` command (any directory or file) and its `stdin` command (e.g. `cat some_file | gitleaks -v stdin`), which covers CI logs piped in or downloaded locally. However, the evidence shows no native connectors for S3 buckets or Docker images. Those sources would have to be synced or extracted to disk, or streamed via other tools, before Gitleaks could scan them. Missing for 10: native S3 bucket scanning, native Docker image/layer scanning, documented CI-log integration, hands-on corroboration of these workflows.
